label: BOSTON • 1919
text: A 15-foot wall of brown liquid came crashing through the streets.

label: A STREET OVERWHELMED
text: It smashed buildings, swept away horses, crushed people, and even damaged an elevated railway.

label: THICK. HEAVY. DIFFICULT TO ESCAPE.
text: People tried to escape, but the liquid was so thick and heavy that getting out of its path was almost impossible.

label: NOT WATER
text:
And the strangest part?

This wasn't a flood of water.

label: NOT AN AVALANCHE
text: It wasn't an avalanche.

label: MOLASSES
text: It was a wave of molasses.

label: JANUARY 15, 1919 • NORTH END
text: On January 15, 1919, an ordinary afternoon in Boston turned into one of the most bizarre disasters in American history.

label: ONE STORAGE TANK
text: And it all began with a giant storage tank that suddenly exploded.

label: 50 FT TALL • 2.3 MILLION GALLONS
text: The tank stood in Boston's North End. It was around 50 feet tall and contained approximately 2.3 million gallons of molasses.

label: NOT JUST PANCAKE SYRUP
text: But this wasn't just some giant container of pancake syrup.

label: MOLASSES → INDUSTRIAL ALCOHOL
text: The molasses was used to produce industrial alcohol, which was needed for everything from liquor to wartime explosives.

label: BUILT IN 1915
text: The company had built the tank just a few years earlier, but there was a serious problem.

label: THE WARNING WAS VISIBLE
text: It leaked.

label: CHILDREN COLLECTED THE LEAKS
text: In fact, molasses regularly seeped through its steel walls. Local children reportedly collected the dripping syrup in buckets.

label: BROWN PAINT, NOT A REPAIR
text: And instead of properly fixing the problem, the company painted the tank brown to hide the leaks.

label: AN ORDINARY JANUARY AFTERNOON
text: Then came that January afternoon.

label: AROUND 12:30 P.M.
text: At around 12:30, people nearby heard a strange rumbling sound.

label: THE STEEL TANK RUPTURED
text: Suddenly, the tank's steel walls began tearing apart. Its rivets burst out like machine-gun fire, and millions of gallons of molasses came crashing into the neighbourhood.

label: REPORTED HEIGHT ≈ 15 FT
text: The wave reportedly reached around 15 feet high and moved at an estimated 35 miles per hour.

label: ESTIMATED 35 MPH • 56 KM/H
text: That's roughly 56 kilometres per hour.

label: FASTER THAN A PERSON COULD RUN
text: Imagine being on a street when a wall of thick, brown liquid comes rushing towards you faster than a car moving through a city.

label: HOMES, STREETS AND LIVELIHOODS
text: Buildings were knocked from their foundations. Horses became trapped. Wooden houses were smashed apart.

label: DAMAGED SUPPORTS • TRAIN STOPPED SHORT
text: The elevated railway was damaged, and an approaching train stopped short of the sagging tracks.

label: ESCAPE WAS NOT SIMPLE
text: And escaping the flood wasn't easy.

label: DENSITY + VISCOSITY
text: Molasses is much denser than water, and its incredible thickness made it extremely difficult for people and animals to move through.

label: COOLING MADE IT THICKER
text: The more some victims struggled, the harder it became to escape.

label: POLICE • FIRE • NAVY • RED CROSS
text: Rescuers rushed in, including police officers, firefighters, sailors and Red Cross workers.

label: RESCUE, ONE PERSON AT A TIME
text: But reaching people trapped beneath the sticky mass was a nightmare.

label: 21 PEOPLE KILLED • ABOUT 150 INJURED
text: By the time the disaster was over, 21 people had lost their lives and around 150 were injured.

label: THIS WAS NOT JUST BAD LUCK
text: But here's where the story gets even more disturbing.

label: A PREVENTABLE STRUCTURAL FAILURE
text: The tank hadn't suddenly failed for no reason.

label: THIN STEEL • INADEQUATE TESTING
text: Investigators discovered that its construction was seriously flawed. Its steel walls were too thin, and the tank had not been properly tested before being put into service.

label: REPEATED LEAKS WERE IGNORED
text: The company had also ignored warning signs, including repeated leaks.

label: THE COMPANY WAS HELD RESPONSIBLE
text: After a long legal battle, the company was held responsible for the disaster.

label: THE CLEANUP TOOK WEEKS
text: And the cleanup was almost as unbelievable as the flood itself.

label: SALT WATER + SAND
text: Workers spent weeks removing molasses from streets, buildings and wreckage. They used salt water to wash away the syrup and spread sand to help absorb it.

label: MOLASSES REACHED THE HARBOR
text: Even the harbour turned brown as the sticky mixture was washed into the water.

label: REVIEW • INSPECTION • ACCOUNTABILITY
text: The disaster eventually helped push Massachusetts towards stricter building regulations and engineering oversight.

label: THE GREAT MOLASSES FLOOD
text: Today, the Great Molasses Flood is remembered as one of the strangest industrial disasters in American history.

label: NOT A NATURAL DISASTER
text: Because sometimes, a disaster doesn't need a hurricane, an earthquake or a tsunami.

label: WARNING SIGNS MATTER
text: Sometimes, all it takes is a badly built tank, millions of gallons of molasses, and a company that ignored the warning signs.
